children: Gold and silver futures settled modestly lower in cautious trading Tuesday, a day ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision, which is widely expected to be a quarter-point rate increase to the 3.75%-4.0% range with further ​tightening signaled.

The continued rally in crude oil prices fueled inflation worries and reinforced expectations that the Fed will raise rates, while benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yields rose to their highest level ​since 2007, and the dollar rose, making greenback-priced bullion more expensive for holders of other currencies.
"Much of the hawkish Fed risk appears ​to be priced in. However, gold could remain vulnerable if policymakers signal ​rates will ⁠stay higher for longer," ING analysts said in a note.

Gold's recent moves suggest little hope that the metal will recapture its role as a haven asset any time soon, TradeNation's David Morrison wrote, as investors have piled back into the dollar and out of gold as the deteriorating Middle East situation and tech leaders' doomsday warnings about AI soured risk sentiment.
